label: common-negative-propagation
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{common-negative-propagation}
For every positive-symbol solution on \(0<\tau\le\tau_b\), at the same
fixed mass in either setting, set \(u=\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-M})\)
and let bars denote actual \(\omega_X\)-means.  Fixed constants give
\[
 \sup u\le\bar u+C_u,\qquad b\ge\bar b-C_b,
 \qquad \sup(-a)\le\overline{-a}+C_a.
\]
They do not assume any of these means bounded and do not require a
global positive lower-arrow norm.
head: environment
name: Negative-potential propagation

title: Proof
body_md:
The independent size numerator and the positive endpoint rows give
\[
 \Delta(-a)\ge-L_0,\quad\Delta(-b)\ge-L_2,
 \quad L_0=\|H_{*0}-\alpha\|_\infty+C_{\rm size},
 \quad L_2=c+C_{\rm size}.
\]
For \(h=e^{-M},\rho=\operatorname{tr}h\), the ordered inverse row and
positive middle forcing imply
\[
 \Delta\rho\ge g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(hf_zhf_{\bar z}h)
                       -(d+C_{\rm size})\rho.
\]
Put \(B_2=h^{1/2}f_zh^{1/2}\).  Then
\(\rho_z=-\operatorname{tr}(hB_2)\) and the positive trace term is
\(\operatorname{tr}(hB_2B_2^*)\).  Weighted Hilbert--Schmidt
Cauchy--Schwarz, for \((A,D)_h=\operatorname{tr}(hAD^*)\), gives
\(|\operatorname{tr}(hB_2)|^2\le\rho\operatorname{tr}(hB_2B_2^*)\).
Thus \(\Delta u\ge-L_1\), \(L_1=d+C_{\rm size}\), without dropping
any moving eigendirection or assigning a sign to an unordered product.

For any real \(U\) with \(\Delta U=s\ge-L\), its source has total
integral zero and \(\|s\|_{L^1}\le2L\operatorname{Vol}X\).
The exact kernel identity gives
\(U(x)-\bar U_{\rm FS}\le Ln_\omega\).
Let \(J(y)=\overline{G_0(\cdot,y)}\), with the actual mean.
Then \(|J(y)|\le n_\omega/(2\pi)\), and averaging the exact identity,
not merely its inequality, gives
\(|\bar U-\bar U_{\rm FS}|\le2Ln_\omega\).
Consequently \(\sup U\le\bar U+3Ln_\omega\).
Apply this to \(-a,-b,u\).  The argument uses only fixed reference
coefficients and positivity, including at a lower-arrow zero.

label: common-scalar-fluctuations
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{common-scalar-fluctuations}
For every fixed finite \(p\ge1\) in either setting,
\[
 \|a-\bar a\|_{L^p}+\|b-\bar b\|_{L^p}+\|u-\bar u\|_{L^p}\le C_p.
\]
In particular \(\int|b-\bar b|\omega_X\le K_b\), with a fixed
parameter-uniform constant.  No \(L^\infty\) fluctuation conclusion is
inferred from this kernel mapping.
head: environment
name: Finite scalar fluctuation bounds

title: Proof
body_md:
For every integer \(k\ge1\), the exact kernel moment is
\(\int|G_0(x,y)|^k\omega_{\rm FS}(x)=(2\pi)^{1-k}k!\), uniformly
in \(y\).  Indeed move \(y\) to \([1:0]\) for this kernel computation;
the squared chordal distance \(s=|z|^2/(1+|z|^2)\) has angularly
integrated measure \(2\pi\,ds\), and
\(\int_0^1(-\log s)^kds=k!\) by \(k\) integrations by parts after
\(s=e^{-v}\).  This does not change the actual source, mean or norm.
For \(H_X(x,y)=G_0(x,y)-\overline{G_0(\cdot,y)}\), Hölder's inequality
for the mean and \(\omega_X\le n_\omega\omega_{\rm FS}\) yield
\[
 \sup_y\|H_X(\cdot,y)\|_{L^k(\omega_X)}
 \le2n_\omega^{1/k}(2\pi)^{1/k-1}(k!)^{1/k}=:C_k'.
\]
The mean-adjusted Green representation and Minkowski give
\(\|U-\bar U\|_{L^k}\le C_k'\|\Delta U\|_{L^1}\).
The source budgets proved in the preceding lemma apply to \(-a,-b,u\).
Every finite real \(p\) follows from an integer \(k\ge p\) and finite
volume Hölder.  In particular one can take
\(K_b=C_1'\,2L_2\operatorname{Vol}X\).
Logarithmic integrability and the distributional kernel identity justify
the same calculation for \(C^{2,\gamma}\) solutions.

label: common-original-endpoint
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{common-original-endpoint}
In either fixed setting suppose that the positive-parameter solutions at
the one fixed finite mass have uniform full values, full first derivatives,
and positive \(q,\beta,V\) gaps on \(0<\tau\le\tau_b\).
Every sequence of such actual solutions with \(\tau_n\downarrow0\) has
a subsequence converging strongly in \(C^{2,\gamma}\) to smooth positive
metrics on the original bundles, with the original maps fixed, solving
the undamped equation, the single normalization, and strict calibration
in all blocks.  Existence at each positive parameter is separately needed
to deduce existence at zero from this assertion.
For the primary application the value input is
Theorem~\ref{primary-value-bound}; for the lower-boundary application it is
Theorem~\ref{lower-value-bound}.  Theorem~\ref{common-gradient-gaps}
then supplies the other uniform bounds, and
Theorem~\ref{common-positive-continuation} independently supplies positive
parameter existence.
head: environment
name: Strong original endpoint and strict calibration

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(\nu=(1+\gamma)/2\) and \(\sigma=(1+\nu)/2\).
In \eqref{common-scalar-principal}, scalar reciprocals are bounded by the
given gaps.  The Lyapunov eigenmultipliers \((v_i+v_j)/2\) are at least
\(\delta_V\), and \(E_M\) and its inverse are smooth with bounded finite
derivatives on the compact bounded value range.  All ordered sources are
smooth in basepoint, values and parameter, and at most quadratic in the
full first derivatives.  The mass is one fixed finite number.  Thus all
six component Laplacians have a uniform two-sided bound, without an
assumed Hölder gradient norm.  Local logarithmic potentials have gradient
modulus \(Ch(1+|\log h|)\); their bounded harmonic remainders have
controlled interior derivatives.  A finite nested atlas gives uniform
\(C^{1,\sigma}\) bounds.  The full smooth source is now uniformly
\(C^{0,\sigma}\), hence \(C^{0,\nu}\).  The zero-circle-mean Hessian
kernel, with the source value subtracted, gives a uniform
\(C^{2,\nu}\) bound as proved in Lemma~\ref{common-local-potentials}.

Ascoli gives a common subsequence converging uniformly through second
derivatives; Hölder interpolation at the strictly lower exponent
\(\gamma\) makes the convergence strong \(C^{2,\gamma}\).
Compactness in the same \(C^{2,\nu}\) norm is not claimed.
The reference chart reconstructs
\(h_0=h_{*0}e^a,h_1=h_{*1}e^M,h_2=h_{*2}e^b\).
Bounded values give uniformly positive upper and lower metric bounds on
the original bundles.  Smooth symbol dependence preserves their gaps.
There is no rank loss or punctured-gauge replacement: the holomorphic maps
and bundle structures have been fixed throughout.

Strong \(C^{2,\gamma}\) passes every curvature, full arrow derivative,
transported adjoint and ordered product.  Bounded values and fixed mass
give \(\tau_n\mu_sB(w_n)w_n\to0\), while \(\tau_nF_*\to0\), so
\(\widehat F(w_0)=0\).  The single integral
\(\int[qa+\operatorname{tr}(VM)+\beta b]\omega_X=0\) passes by uniform
value convergence.  No separate vertex mean is inserted.
In the boundary setting every coefficient remains smooth at the section
zero and at coincidence of the two divisors: \(D\psi\) is retained and
no coefficient divides by \(\psi,r\), the composition, or a normalized
lower arrow.  This is the zero-safe regularity check, not a transfer of
the primary lower-norm argument.

At zero the scalar-principal equation is smooth.  Starting with
\(C^{2,\gamma}\), its source is \(C^{1,\gamma}\); differentiated local
Poisson/cutoff estimates give \(C^{3,\gamma}\).  Repeating at each finite
order makes all fields and metrics smooth.
At the zero-parameter endpoint write \(q^{(0)}=q(w_0)\).
The exact undamped rows are
\[
 q^{(0)}(H_0-\alpha)=A_0+K_0,\quad
 \mathcal L_{V_0}(\widehat H_1-\alpha I)=A_0I+K_1,\quad
 \beta_0(H_2-\alpha)=A_0+K_2.
\]
The endpoint rows imply \(H_0,H_2>\alpha\).  The ordered positive
Lyapunov inverse has \(\mathcal L_{V_0}^{-1}(A_0I)=A_0V_0^{-1}>0\),
so \(\widehat H_1>\alpha I\) without commutation.
The frozen vertical coefficients are
\(S_0=q^{(0)}+\alpha,S_1=V_0+\alpha I,S_2=\beta_0+\alpha\).
Thus the phase coefficient \(\mathcal B_j=H_j+S_j\) satisfies
\(\mathcal B_j>2\alpha I=I/3\) in every block.
For the frozen \(\theta_4=\pi-\arctan6\),
\(\sin\theta_4=6/\sqrt{37}>0\), and the exact phase equation is
\(\cos\theta_4\mathcal B_j=\sin\theta_4\mathcal A_j\).
Consequently
\[
 \cos\theta_4\mathcal A_j+\sin\theta_4\mathcal B_j
 =\mathcal B_j/\sin\theta_4>\sqrt{37}\,I/18.
\]
This proves strict calibration at the smooth undamped endpoint,
not at a forced auxiliary solution.

label: primary-value-bound
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{primary-value-bound}
For every normalized $C^{2,\gamma}$ solution in the full chart
$w=(a,M,b)$, where $M$ is a Hermitian $2\times2$ field, with
$0<\tau\le\tau_b$ and $q,\beta,V>0$, there is a bound
\[
 \|a\|_\infty+\|b\|_\infty+\|M\|_{\mathrm{op},\infty}\le B.
\]
Here $B$ depends only on the fixed original primary, its reference,
background, mass, and interval, and is independent of $\tau$, the
solution, and its symbol minima.
head: environment
name: Fixed-chain value bound

title: Proof
body_md:
Every unbounded sequence would admit the normalized extraction above.
Isotropic escape is excluded by the bottom row, the two degree-one
spectral exclusions reduce anisotropic escape exactly to
\eqref{primary-residual-alternatives}, and the reciprocal allocations
exclude both alternatives. Thus the middle mean in
\eqref{primary-one-mean} is bounded uniformly. The reconstruction
\eqref{primary-value-reconstruction} bounds both endpoints and both
middle eigenvalues, proving the full field bound.

label: primary-existence
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{primary-existence}
Every original primary chain admits a smooth positive Hermitian metric
triple solving the frozen reduced dHYM equation at
$\theta_4=\pi-\arctan6$ and satisfying its strict calibration inequality
in all three blocks.
head: environment
name: Primary existence

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix the chain. Keep its same reference, one exponent $\gamma\in(0,1)$,
and the single prospectively chosen finite strong mass $\mu_s$.
The construction of \ref{common-positive-continuation} gives actual
normalized smooth positive-symbol solutions at every $\tau\in(0,1]$.
Theorem \ref{primary-value-bound} bounds every such solution on
$(0,\tau_b]$. On precisely this interval the middle force satisfies
$C_1^\tau\ge A_0I/2$. Therefore the values-conditioned estimate
\ref{common-gradient-gaps}, with $B$ from
Theorem \ref{primary-value-bound} and $c_1=A_0/2$, gives a uniform full
reference gradient bound and positive constants
\[
 q\ge\delta_q,\qquad\beta\ge\delta_\beta,\qquad V\ge\delta_VI
\]
for these same solutions. All its fields, reference residuals, and
normalization agree with \eqref{primary-rows}. The lower reference norm
is positive because the original lower arrow is nonvanishing; a
pointwise nonzero composition is not required.

Choose any sequence $\tau_n\downarrow0$ in $(0,\tau_b]$ and a solution
at each parameter. At the same fixed reference and finite mass, the
preceding values, gradients and symbol gaps satisfy
Theorem~\ref{common-original-endpoint}. It gives a subsequence
converging strongly in $C^{2,\gamma}$ in the original chart,
reconstructs smooth positive metrics on the original bundles with their
maps fixed, and preserves the single normalization. The damping and
reference-forcing terms vanish because the mass is fixed and the values
are bounded. The theorem's ordered endpoint rows and phase calculation
then give the undamped equation and strict calibration in all three

head: environment

label: lower-mean-transfer
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lower-mean-transfer}
Under \eqref{lower-green-u}--\eqref{lower-radial-upper}, all six
real field values are bounded uniformly on the fixed positive
parameter slab if and only if $L_0$ is bounded above there.
More precisely, there is a fixed $C_-$ such that
\[
 a,b\ge-L_0-C_-,\qquad M\ge-(L_0+C_-)I.
\]
If $L_0$ tends to $+\infty$ along a sequence, then
\[
 \|a\|_\infty+\|b\|_\infty+\|M\|_{\mathrm{op},\infty}
       \le C(1+L_0)
\]
along its tail.  Constants may depend on the fixed chain and
reference; no uniformity across varying chains is asserted.
head: environment
name: Positive-area transfer of the lower mean

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $m=\lambda_{\min}(M)$.  Since $u\ge-m$,
\eqref{lower-green-u} gives $m\ge-L_0-C_u$.
Functional calculus and the positive trace pairing give
\[
 p_1\le p_*e^{a-m}.
\]
Using $p_1>\alpha$ we obtain
\[
 a\ge-L_0-C_u-\log(p_*/\alpha).
\]

The reference lower arrow is not identically zero.  Consequently
\[
 r_\Omega=\frac12\max_Xr_*>0,\qquad
 \Omega=\{r_*>r_\Omega\},\qquad
 m_\Omega=\int_\Omega\omega_X>0.
\]
This set is fixed independently of the solution and parameter.
On $\Omega$,
\[
 r=e^{-b}\operatorname{tr}(P_*e^M)
       \ge r_\Omega e^{m-b}.
\]
The inequality $r<d$ therefore implies
\[
 b\ge-L_0-C_\Omega\quad\hbox{on }\Omega,
 \qquad C_\Omega=C_u+\log(d/r_\Omega).
\]
Integrating over $\Omega$ and using the fluctuation estimate gives
\begin{align*}
 m_\Omega\overline b
 &=\int_\Omega b\,\omega_X
       -\int_\Omega(b-\overline b)\,\omega_X\\
 &\ge m_\Omega(-L_0-C_\Omega)-K_b.
\end{align*}
It follows from \eqref{lower-green-b} that
\[
 b\ge-L_0-C_\Omega-K_b/m_\Omega-C_b
       \quad\hbox{everywhere on }X.
\]
Enlarge a nonnegative $C_-$ to cover all three lower bounds.
No estimate has divided by the lower arrow at $p$.

Suppose $L_0\le B_1$ and put $D=\max\{0,B_1+C_-\}$.
The shifted scalars and matrix are nonnegative.  The reference
weights satisfy
\[
 q_*,\beta_*\ge\delta,\quad V_*\ge\delta I,
 \quad \delta=\frac4{21},\qquad
 q_*+\operatorname{tr}V_*+\beta_*=W=\frac{10}{3}.
\]
Thus \eqref{lower-radial-upper} implies
\[
 \delta\bigl((a+D)+\operatorname{tr}(M+DI)+(b+D)\bigr)
       \le C_T+DW.
\]
Each nonnegative summand, including each shifted eigenvalue of
$M$, is bounded by this sum.  This proves the full value bound.
Conversely, $\|M\|_{\mathrm{op},\infty}\le B$ gives
$u\le B+\log2$ and hence $L_0\le B+\log2$.
Finally use $D=L_0+C_-$ on a tail where it is nonnegative in the
same calculation to obtain the asserted linear escape bound.
head: environment

label: lower-residual-extraction
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lower-residual-extraction}
If the original solution family has unbounded full values, a common
subsequence has $L_n=\overline u_n\to\infty$, $t_n\to0$,
$\tau_n\to0$, and $t_nL_n\to\rho\ge0$, with
\begin{equation}\label{lower-residual-profiles}
 a_n/L_n,\ b_n/L_n,\ m_n/L_n\to-1,\qquad
 n_n/L_n\to\vartheta>-1
\end{equation}
strongly in every finite $L^s$ and almost everywhere.  Moreover
$\|w_n\|_\infty\le C(1+L_n)$, and smooth nonincreasing low spectral
probes $E_n=\chi(M_n/L_n)$ converge strongly in $L^2$, weakly in $H^1$,
to the constant reference projection $\Pi_L$ onto $L$.
The escape parameter $\vartheta$ is distinct from the phase $\theta_4$.
head: environment
name: The only possible normalized escape

title: Proof
body_md:
Lemma~\ref{lower-mean-transfer} gives $L_n\to\infty$ and the full
linear value bound after selecting solutions with increasing values.
The size estimate gives $t_n(L_n-\log2)\le\mathcal C$; hence
$t_n\to0$ and $\tau_n=t_n/\mu_s\to0$ because the mass is fixed.
Extract $t_nL_n\to\rho$ and the finitely many normalized means.
The fluctuation bounds give
\[
 a_n/L_n\to A,\quad b_n/L_n\to B,\quad
 m_n/L_n\to-1,\quad n_n/L_n\to\vartheta\ge-1.
\]
All convergence is strong in finite $L^s$ and almost everywhere.
The lower bounds give $A,B\ge-1$.  Since
$p_1\ge p_*e^{a-n}$ and $p_1<8/3$,
$a\le n+\log(112/27)$, so $A\le\vartheta$.

The flat reference gives the ordered energy identity
\begin{equation}\label{lower-logarithmic-energy}
 \int g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(M_{\bar z}f^{-1}f_z)
    =\int\operatorname{tr}[M(\widehat H_1-2I)]\ge0.
\end{equation}
In an $M$-eigenbasis its integrand has coefficients
$k_{\exp}(s)=(e^s-1)/s$, with value $1$ at zero and
$k_{\exp}(s)\ge(1+|s|)^{-1}$.  The curvature budget bounds the
energy by $C\|M\|_\infty$, whence
\[
 \int|DM|^2\le C\|M\|_\infty(1+2\|M\|_\infty).
\]
Thus $M_n/L_n$ is $H^1$ bounded.  Local mollification has error
$C\varepsilon\|D(M_n/L_n)\|_2$; fixed mollifications have a
finite-grid convergent subsequence.  A diagonal choice as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives strong $L^2$, weak $H^1$ compactness.

If $\vartheta=-1$, then $A=-1$.  The normalized radial entropy
\[
 (v-T)/L_n=L_n^{-1}\{
 \operatorname{tr}[R_*k(aI-M)]+
 \operatorname{tr}[P_*k(M-bI)]\},\quad
 k(y)=ye^y-e^y+1,
\]
tends to zero almost everywhere.  The upper normalized arguments
tend to zero, and the lower ones tend to $-1-B\le0$.
The bounded exponential sums $p_1<8/3$, $r<d$, together with the
normalized value bound, dominate these terms, also where $P_*=0$.
Since $\overline v=0$, the limiting trace equation yields
$0=\alpha-2c+dB$, or $B=9/11$.
The upper bound for $T$ and $a\le n+\log(112/27)$ give
$(c-\alpha)n+cm+db\le C$.  The global lower bounds for $m$ and
$b\ge\overline b-C_b$ imply $n\le-L_n+o(L_n)$ uniformly.
Therefore
\[
 r_n\le\max r_*\,e^{n_n-b_n}
       \le C e^{-(20/11+o(1))L_n}\to0
\]
uniformly.  The actual lower Bochner identity
\[
 2\int K_2=\int\operatorname{tr}(P\widehat H_1)-\int rH_2
\]
and the current-curvature budgets give $\int K_2\to0$.
Integrating the undivided bottom row gives
$dc\mathcal V+dt_n\int b_n=A_0\mathcal V+o(1)$, hence
$t_n\overline b_n\to-3/11$.  This contradicts $B=9/11$ and $t_n>0$.

Now $\vartheta>-1$.  The matrix limit is
$-\Pi+\vartheta(I-\Pi)$ for a rank-one Hermitian $H^1$ projection.
Choose a fixed smooth nonincreasing $\chi$ equal to $1$ near $-1$
and $0$ near $\vartheta$.  Smooth divided differences at repeated
spectra make $E_n=\chi(M_n/L_n)$ $H^1$ bounded and strongly $L^2$
convergent to $\Pi$.  The exact moving test is
\begin{equation}\label{lower-spectral-test}
 \int\operatorname{tr}(E_n\widehat H_{1,n})
 =2\int\operatorname{tr}E_n+
      \int g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}[(E_n)_{\bar z}f_n^{-1}(f_n)_z].
\end{equation}
Every coefficient in the last integrand is a nonpositive divided
difference of $\chi$, multiplied by a positive exponential divided
difference.  On the good set where the normalized eigenvalues lie
in their separated plateaus, retain its $21$ term:
\[
 \int g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}[(E_n)_{\bar z}f_n^{-1}(f_n)_z]
 \le-\int_{\rm good}g^{-1}(1-e^{-(n_n-m_n)})
                         |(E_n)_z{}_{21}|^2.
\]
The bad set has vanishing measure; its terms are discarded with
their nonpositive sign.  The $L^2$-bounded fields
$(I-E_n)(E_n)_zE_n$ converge weakly to $(I-\Pi)\Pi_z\Pi$.
Multiplication by the good-set indicator preserves this weak limit:
pair a fixed $L^2$ test with the bad set and use its vanishing
$L^2$ norm there.  Weak lower semicontinuity therefore gives
\begin{equation}\label{lower-spectral-degree}
 \limsup\overline{\operatorname{tr}(E_n\widehat H_{1,n})}
       \le2-\mathfrak E_\Pi/\mathcal V,
 \qquad \mathfrak E_\Pi=\int g^{-1}|(I-\Pi)\Pi_z\Pi|^2.
\end{equation}

Bounded arrow values on the good set give the implications
\[
 A>-1\Longrightarrow\phi\Pi=0,\qquad
 B<\vartheta\Longrightarrow(I-\Pi)\psi=0.
\]
For example a strict normalized exponential gap forces the corresponding
reference arrow coefficient to zero; strong $L^2$ probe convergence
then passes that bounded coefficient.  Both constraints cannot hold,
because $\phi\psi$ is nonzero.  If $A>-1$, then
$\Pi=\Pi_{\ker\phi}$ and $B\ge\vartheta>-1$.
The kernel is the smooth holomorphic $\mathcal O(1)$ line; its
reference Gauss--Codazzi degree identity gives $\mathfrak E_\Pi=\mathcal V$.
Thus \eqref{lower-spectral-degree} has upper bound $1$.
On the other hand its low-$P$ values tend to zero in $L^1$, and
\[
 V^{-1}\ge(cI+P)^{-1}=c^{-1}I-P/[c(c+r)].
\]
The positive bare force and reciprocal budget give the lower bound
$\alpha+\rho+A_0/c=7/5+\rho$, a contradiction.  Therefore $A=-1$.

If $B>-1$, bounded high-$R$ and low-$P$ values tend to zero in $L^1$.
Hence $\overline{q+\operatorname{tr}(E_nV)}\to c-\alpha=2/3$.
The spectral test and the top degree give
\[
 \limsup\overline{\operatorname{tr}(E_nD_n)}\le d-\rho,
 \qquad\overline U_{0,n}\to17/6-\rho.
\]
For any positive $E$, scalar--matrix Hilbert Cauchy gives
\begin{equation}\label{lower-hilbert-cauchy}
 (1+\overline{\operatorname{tr}E})^2
 \le\overline{q+\operatorname{tr}(EV)}\,
       \overline{q^{-1}+\operatorname{tr}(EV^{-1})}.
\end{equation}
Use the Hilbert vectors $E^{1/2}V^{1/2}$ and $E^{1/2}V^{-1/2}$
and cyclic trace, together with $q^{1/2},q^{-1/2}$ in the scalar
slot.  No $EV=VE$ is required.  Since $C_j^\tau\to A_0I_j$,
the reciprocal budgets absorb the force errors.  The lower
top-plus-middle source bound is $4A_0/(2/3)=37/6$, whereas its
upper bound is $17/6+d-2\rho\le28/6$.  This contradiction excludes
every $B>-1$.  We have $B=-1<\vartheta$, so the lower-arrow
constraint identifies $\Pi=\Pi_L$ off $p$, hence almost everywhere
with the constant reference projection onto the saturated $\mathcal O(2)$
line.  This proves the stated exhaustive residual.
head: environment

label: lower-divisor-atoms
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lower-divisor-atoms}
On a common measure subsequence, let
\[
 \mathfrak a_0,\quad\mathfrak a_L,\quad
 \mathfrak a_Q,\quad\mathfrak a_2
\]
be the scalar curvature atoms at $q_0$, and let $\mathfrak a_m$ be the
atom of the distribution $2-\Delta m_\infty$.  Then
\begin{equation}\label{lower-atom-laws}
\begin{gathered}
 \mathfrak a_m=\mathfrak a_0-\mathcal V\ge0,\qquad
 \mathfrak a_L\ge\mathfrak a_m,\qquad
 \mathfrak a_L,\mathfrak a_Q,\mathfrak a_2\ge0,\\
 \alpha\mathfrak a_0=c(\mathfrak a_L+\mathfrak a_Q)
                                      +d\mathfrak a_2,\qquad
 \mathcal V\le\mathfrak a_0\le\tfrac54\mathcal V.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
For $p\ne q_0$, also $\mathfrak a_2\ge\mathfrak a_L$ and
$\mathfrak a_0\le(16/15)\mathcal V$.
For $p=q_0$, the valid comparison is
$\mathfrak a_L\le\mathfrak a_2+\mathcal V$.
head: environment
name: Mandatory original divisor atoms

title: Proof
body_md:
The uniform scalar Laplacian total variations give strong compactness of
centered potentials in every finite $L^s$.  To see this for the actual
Green kernel, truncate the chordal logarithm to a continuous bounded
kernel.  Its omitted $L^s$ tail tends to zero uniformly in the source
point, because
$\int|G_0|^k\omega_{\rm FS}=(2\pi)^{1-k}k!$.
Minkowski controls this omitted potential for bounded-variation measures;
weak measure convergence gives uniform convergence for the truncated
kernel.  Subtracting the actual means preserves the argument.
For $m=-u+\epsilon$, the normalized spectral separation makes
$\epsilon_n\to0$ in finite $L^s$; thus the same compactness applies
to $m$.  Extract the bounded relative-mean differences as well.

The bounded high-$R$ values disappear.  The limiting upper norm is
therefore
\[
 p_{1,\infty}=e^{a_\infty-m_\infty+\delta_a}u_*,\qquad
 \alpha\le p_{1,\infty}\le8/3,
\]
where $\delta_a=\lim(\bar a-\bar m)$.
Its exact logarithmic Bochner identity is
\begin{equation}\label{lower-upper-log-bochner}
 \Delta\log p_1=\operatorname{tr}(J\widehat H_1)-H_0+\kappa_K.
\end{equation}
The curvature and kinetic budgets bound its Laplacian variation.
Its bounded limiting logarithm has no Laplacian atom.  Indeed a
finite-measure Laplacian atom of mass $\lambda$ produces circular
average $(\lambda/2\pi)\log r^2+o(|\log r|)$ by the logarithmic
kernel; dominated convergence handles the non-atomic remainder.
A bounded potential therefore has no atom, and a potential bounded
below has nonpositive Laplacian atoms, or nonnegative curvature atoms.

The identity
$m_\infty=a_\infty+\delta_a+\log u_*-\log p_{1,\infty}$
has the original simple divisor $\mathcal V\delta_{q_0}$ and gives
$\mathfrak a_m=\mathfrak a_0-\mathcal V$.
The centered lower bounds make all displayed curvature atoms
nonnegative.  Since $\ell_L\ge m$ with bounded relative means,
the same circular-average comparison gives
$\mathfrak a_L\ge\mathfrak a_m$.
The bounded trace combination has no atom, giving the linear atom law.
It implies $(c-\alpha)\mathfrak a_0\le c\mathcal V$, hence the
upper bound $5\mathcal V/4$.

If $p\ne q_0$, $r_*>0$ near $q_0$, and
$b-\ell_L\ge\log(r_*/d)$ there.  Thus
$\mathfrak a_2\ge\mathfrak a_L\ge\mathfrak a_0-\mathcal V$;
the linear law gives
$(c+d-\alpha)\mathfrak a_0\le(c+d)\mathcal V$,
or $\mathfrak a_0\le16\mathcal V/15$.
If $p=q_0$, the simple lower divisor instead permits
$\mathfrak a_L\le\mathfrak a_2+\mathcal V$.
The estimates \eqref{lower-logarithmic-values} give bounded centered
potentials off $q_0$, so the positive scalar-source atoms are localized
there.  This does not yet exclude non-atomic concentration.

For later comparisons retain the actual product atom
$\mathfrak b_R$ of $\operatorname{tr}(J\widehat H_1)\omega_X$.
Positivity of $D$ and bounded damping imply
$0\le\mathfrak b_R\le\mathfrak a_L+\mathfrak a_Q$.
Taking atoms in \eqref{lower-upper-log-bochner} gives
\begin{equation}\label{lower-kernel-atom}
 \mathfrak k_K=\mathfrak a_0-\mathfrak b_R
 \ge\tfrac45\mathfrak a_0+\tfrac{11}{5}\mathfrak a_2
 \ge\tfrac45\mathcal V.
\end{equation}
This is a moving-product measure identity, not a product of limits.
head: environment

label: lower-local-gradient-gaps
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lower-local-gradient-gaps}
For every $K\Subset X^\circ$, the fields of
\eqref{lower-transformed-equations} satisfy
\[
 |\nabla A_n|+\|\nabla F_n\|+|\nabla B_n|\le C_K,
 \qquad q_n\ge\delta_{q,K}>0,\quad
 \beta_n\ge\delta_{\beta,K}>0,\quad V_n\ge\delta_{V,K}I.
\]
Constants depend on the fixed data and nested buffers, but not on the
escaping means or the original symbol minima.
head: environment
name: Full local first derivatives and all symbol gaps

label: lower-local-density
title: Proof
body_md:
Choose $K\Subset K^+\Subset X^\circ$ and on $K^+$ let
$c_FI\le F_n\le C_FI$, $|A_n|+|B_n|\le B_F$.
Put $h_n=F_n^{-1}$, $\mathcal U=\operatorname{tr}V^{-1}$,
$\mathcal W_1=\operatorname{tr}(V^{-1}K_1)$.
Ordered inverse differentiation gives
\[
 \Delta h_n=g^{-1}h_n(F_n)_zh_n(F_n)_{\bar z}h_n
       -dh_n-\Psi_nh_n
       +S_n^{-1}\mathcal L_V^{-1}(\widetilde C_{1,n}+K_1)S_n^{-1}.
\]
Its trace obeys
\[
 \Delta\operatorname{tr}h_n\ge
       a_F|\nabla F_n|^2+C_F^{-1}\mathcal W_1
           +(A_0/2)C_F^{-1}\mathcal U-C.
\]
For $|\nabla F|^2=2\|F_z\|_{\rm HS}^2/g$, take
$a_F=1/(2C_F^3)$.
The bounded scalar potential
$\Phi_n=\operatorname{tr}F_n^{-1}-A_n+e^{-B_n}$ controls every
gradient.  Indeed
\[
 \Delta e^{-B_n}=e^{-B_n}
 \{ -c-b_n^d+(C_2^{\tau_n}+K_2)/\beta+|(B_n)_z|^2/g\},
\]
and \eqref{lower-transformed-jets}, with $p_1>\alpha$, gives
$|\nabla A_n|^2\le C(K_0+|\nabla F_n|^2+1)$.
Since $V\le(c+d)I$,
$\mathcal W_1\ge(K_0+K_2)/(c+d)$.
The top row and these inequalities yield
\begin{equation}\label{lower-local-density}
 \Delta\Phi_n\ge a\mathcal F_n-C,\quad a>0,\qquad
 \mathcal F_n=|\nabla A_n|^2+|\nabla F_n|^2+|\nabla B_n|^2
     +\mathcal U+\mathcal W_1+q^{-1}+K_0/q+\beta^{-1}+K_2/\beta.
\end{equation}
The full bottom gradient is controlled even when $v=0$.
Dirichlet Green on the same fixed-radius disk $D_{r_0}(z)$ for every
center in a smaller buffer gives
\begin{equation}\label{lower-all-center-log-bound}
 \int_{D_{r_0}(z)}\log\frac{r_0}{|y-z|}\mathcal F_n\,\omega_X\le H,
 \qquad \int_{D_s(z)}\mathcal F_n\,\omega_X
                   \le\frac H{\log(r_0/s)}\to0.
\end{equation}
The full component rows also give
$|\Delta A_n|+|\Delta B_n|+\|\Delta F_n\|\le C(1+\mathcal F_n)$.

Suppose gradients fail to be bounded.  In a fixed interior disk maximize
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z,\partial D)
       |\nabla(A_n,F_n,B_n)(z)|.
\]
At the chosen point $z_n$ let the gradient be $G_n^\nabla\to\infty$.
Then the distance times $G_n^\nabla$ tends to infinity, and gradients
are at most $2G_n^\nabla$ on the half-distance disk.
The first-scale fields at $z_n+y/G_n^\nabla$ have bounded values and
Lipschitz constants on expanding disks.  Equation
\eqref{lower-all-center-log-bound} makes their energy on every fixed
disk tend to zero; every locally uniform limit is constant.
Derivative convergence still needs the complete face equations.

Set $T_R=\mathcal L_V^{-1}R$, $T_P=\mathcal L_V^{-1}P$, and
$N=\widetilde C_1+K_1$.  The scalar symbol rows are
\begin{equation}\label{lower-local-scalar-rows}
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta q&=(2-p_1/q)K_0+\operatorname{tr}(T_RN)-p_1C_0/q
                       +\mathcal R_q,\\
 \Delta\beta&=-(2+r/\beta)K_2+\operatorname{tr}(T_PN)-rC_2/\beta
                       +\mathcal R_\beta,\\
 \mathcal R_q&=p_1a^d-\operatorname{tr}(R\widehat\Psi),\qquad
 \mathcal R_\beta=rb^d-\operatorname{tr}(P\widehat\Psi).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
All remainders are uniformly bounded coefficient functions.
At every point $V\ge(2/3-q)I$ and $\lambda_{\max}V\ge c$.
This leaves precisely strict interior, strict-$V$ scalar faces, pure
matrix face, or mixed matrix/bottom face.

In strict interior all component first-scale Laplacians are two-sided
bounded.  The local Poisson compactness of
Lemma~\ref{common-local-potentials} gives $C^1$ convergence to the
constant value limit, contradicting the unit gradient witness.
If $V$ is strict, the middle derivatives first vanish; strict endpoints
also have vanishing normalized derivative.  A collapsing scalar therefore
preserves $q_z/G_n^\nabla=p_1(A_n)_z/G_n^\nabla+o(1)$ or
$\beta_z/G_n^\nabla=r(B_n)_z/G_n^\nabla+o(1)$.
For a beta face $r=d-\beta\to d$, so no global lower norm is needed.
For $q\le1/18$, $V\ge11I/18$.  The transforms with
\[
 F_q'(q)=\frac{\sqrt q}{\alpha+q},\qquad
 F_b'(\beta)=\frac{\sqrt\beta}{d-\beta}
\]
cancel the singular parallel kinetics in
\eqref{lower-local-scalar-rows}.  The upper perpendicular coefficient
is at most $-18/11$; the beta perpendicular terms also have the
required nonpositive sign.  Thus
\[
 \Delta F_q\le C\sqrt q(1+(G_n^\nabla)^2),\qquad
 \Delta F_b\le C\sqrt\beta(1+(G_n^\nabla)^2).
\]
For the collapsing symbol $s$, use its amplitude scale
$\ell_n=s(z_n)/G_n^\nabla$.  The positive Lipschitz ratio
$Q_n(y)=s(z_n+\ell_ny)/s(z_n)$ has $Q_n(0)=1$.
The normalized transform converges to a positive multiple of
$Q^{3/2}$ with nonpositive distributional Laplacian on the plane.
A nonnegative entire superharmonic function is constant: convolve,
use the circular mean to exclude positive $-\Delta$ mass, and then
use differentiated Poisson estimates on arbitrarily large disks.
Hence $Q=1$.  On the derived disk $Q_n\ge1/2$ the exact row has
bounded two-sided normalized Laplacians, so Poisson $C^1$ compactness
contradicts the preserved symbol derivative.  Simultaneous scalar
collapse is covered by the same argument for either witness.

For the matrix face let $\lambda=\lambda_{\min}V<c/4$,
$\nu=\lambda_{\max}V$.  Then $q\ge11/24$,
$\nu\ge c$, $\nu-\lambda\ge3c/4$.
In its separated eigenframe write
$\rho_1=R_{ee}$, $\pi_1=P_{ee}$,
$\zeta_1=R_{ef}=P_{ef}$, $s_1=\rho_1+\pi_1$.
The full eigenvalue row is
\begin{equation}\label{lower-local-matrix-row}
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta\lambda={}&(|y_1|^2-|x_1|^2)/g
       +\rho_1(C_0+K_0)/q+\pi_1(C_2+K_2)/\beta\\
 &-s_1N_{ee}/\lambda
       -4\operatorname{Re}(\zeta_1N_{fe})/(\lambda+\nu)
       +\mathcal R_\lambda-\mathcal C_{\rm eig},\\
 \mathcal R_\lambda={}&
 [\mathcal L_{R+P}\widehat\Psi-a^dR-b^dP]_{ee},\\
 \mathcal C_{\rm eig}={}&
 \frac{|u_1x_2-y_1\bar v_2|^2+|u_2x_1-y_2\bar v_1|^2}
                  {g(\nu-\lambda)}\ge0.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Both eigenvalue-concavity squares and the common-connection mixed
term are retained.
When $\beta$ is strict the whole singular image of the six-component
row is $-m_fN_f$, with
$m_f=N_{ee}/\lambda$ and $N_f=(0,S_n\Pi_eS_n,0)$.
Five smooth covectors annihilate this moving image exactly.
Differentiating their pairings with $w_z$ kills the singular source
before it is estimated; their coefficient derivatives give bounded
quadratics on the first scale.  This is the moving-annihilator
calculation of \eqref{common-moving-annihilator}, with the bounded
transformed remainders just displayed.  Cauchy-kernel compactness makes
all five projected derivatives tend uniformly to zero, since the
first-scale value limit is constant.  As
$d\lambda(N_f)=s_1\ge c-\lambda$, a nonzero lambda derivative
witness remains.  Equation~\eqref{lower-local-matrix-row} gives
\[
 \Delta\lambda\le-\frac{|\lambda_z|^2}{2g\lambda}
                        +C(1+(G_n^\nabla)^2).
\]
The $\lambda^{3/2}$ transform at scale $\lambda(z_n)/G_n^\nabla$
again gives the constant amplitude limit; the exact two-sided row
contradicts the witness.  Nothing here requires $P>0$ at $p$.

On the mixed face the two singular images are
$-m_fN_f-m_bN_b$, where $m_b=(C_2+K_2)/\beta$,
$N_b=(0,0,1)$.  Four smooth covectors kill both images at every
moving state; the bounded non-exact quadratic terms remain in their
$\bar\partial$ sources.  Their projected derivatives tend to zero.
The remaining differential frame is
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}d\lambda(N_f)&d\lambda(N_b)\\
                 d\beta(N_f)&d\beta(N_b)\end{pmatrix}
 =\begin{pmatrix}s_1&-\pi_1\\-\pi_1&r\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad\det\ge(3c/4)(d/2)=55/96.
\]
For $1<j<2$ put $s_j=\lambda+j\beta$.
The full combined row is
\begin{equation}\label{lower-local-combined-row}
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta s_j={}&-(s_1-j\pi_1)N_{ee}/\lambda
             -(jr-\pi_1)(C_2+K_2)/\beta\\
 &+(|y_1|^2-|x_1|^2)/g-2jK_2+\rho_1(C_0+K_0)/q\\
 &+jP_{ff}N_{ff}/\nu
       +4(j-1)\operatorname{Re}(\zeta_1N_{fe})/(\lambda+\nu)\\
 &+\mathcal R_\lambda+j\mathcal R_\beta-\mathcal C_{\rm eig}.
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For $j=5/4,7/4$, $s_1-j\pi_1\ge5/8$ and
$jr-\pi_1\ge(j-1)d/2$.  The derivative formula and three-term
square inequality therefore give the common sufficient constant
\[
 \Delta s_j\le-\frac{|(s_j)_z|^2}{60g s_j}
                       +C(1+(G_n^\nabla)^2),\qquad
 \Delta s_j^{61/60}\le C s_j^{1/60}(1+(G_n^\nabla)^2).
\]
Use the shared scale
$\delta_n=\lambda(z_n)+\beta(z_n)$,
$\ell_n=\delta_n/G_n^\nabla$.  Entire superharmonic Liouville makes
both transformed amplitudes constant, hence
$\lambda/\delta_n\to L$, $\beta/\delta_n\to B$, $L+B=1$.
The four annihilator projections and the invertible frame also give
$(w(z_n+\ell_ny)-w(z_n))/\delta_n\to0$ locally uniformly.
If $L,B>0$, both relative denominators are buffered and two-sided
Poisson compactness contradicts the gradient witness.
If $L=0,B=1$, five covectors killing $N_f$ preserve a lambda witness.
On its smaller scale $\lambda(z_n)/G_n^\nabla$, beta is comparable
to $\delta_n$ and the transformed lambda error carries
$\lambda(z_n)/\beta\to0$; its exact two-sided row gives the contradiction.
If $B=0,L=1$, the $A,F$ derivatives vanish by their bounded sources;
the witness is in $B_n$, hence $\beta_z/G_n^\nabla$ because $r\to d$.
On the smaller beta scale lambda is comparable to $\delta_n$, and the
error carries $\beta(z_n)/\lambda\to0$.  The beta row gives the
contradiction.  No unproved relative-error rate is divided by a vanishing
symbol.  This exhausts the faces and proves the full interior gradient bound.

To obtain gaps without a global minimizing center, use the elementary
circular-mean lemma.  If positive $C^2$ functions on a fixed disk have
$|\nabla s_n|\le L\ge1$, $\Delta_{\mathbb R^2}s_n\le C-c/s_n$,
and $s_n(0)=\epsilon_n\to0$, then $s_n(y)\le\epsilon_n+L|y|$.
Their circular means satisfy
\[
 m_n(r)\le\epsilon_n+Cr^2/4
       -c\int_0^r\log(r/u)\frac u{\epsilon_n+Lu}\,du.
\]
For fixed $r$ its upper limit is $Cr^2/4-cr/L<0$ when $r$ is
sufficiently small, contradicting positivity.  The fixed conformal
factor converts the $\Delta_X$ inequalities to this form.
Insert nested buffers $K\Subset K_1\Subset K_2\Subset K^+$.
The proved gradient bound on $K_2$ bounds every kinetic and all symbol
Lipschitz constants.  For $q\le1/18$ the scalar row gives
$\Delta q\le C-\alpha(55/63)/q$, proving a q-gap on $K_1$.
First prove the same-point combined gap for $s=\lambda+\tfrac32\beta$:
on its small separated chart the combined row gives
\[
 \Delta s\le C-\frac{(5/8)(A_0/2)}\lambda
                -\frac{(d/4)A_0}\beta\le C-c_s/s.
\]
Thus $s\ge\delta_s>0$ on $K_1$.
A small lambda at a center in $K$ stays small on a fixed Lipschitz
disk in $K_1$; there $\beta\ge\delta_s/3$, and
$\Delta\lambda\le C-(3c/4)(A_0/2)/\lambda$ gives the matrix gap.
A small beta center instead has $\lambda\ge\delta_s/2$ and
$r\ge d/2$ on its disk; the beta row gives
$\Delta\beta\le C-(d/2)A_0/\beta$.
Different centers have never been synchronized; repeated matrix spectra
are avoided only on the small-lambda separated chart where they cannot
occur.  All three local gaps follow.

label: lower-strong-punctured-limit
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lower-strong-punctured-limit}
A common subsequence converges strongly in $C^{2,\gamma'}$ on every
compact subset of $X^\circ$, for each fixed $0<\gamma'<1$, to full
positive Hermitian $F$ and scalar fields $A,B$.
The limiting arrows are $(\phi_L,0)$ and $(\sigma,0)^T$ and their
actual covariant derivatives are retained.  In current unitary frames
the limit satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{lower-punctured-rows}
\begin{gathered}
 R=p_1J,\quad P=vv^*=r\Pi,\quad q=p_1-\alpha,\quad
 \beta=d-r,\quad V=cI-R+P,\quad K=I-J,\\
 U_0=(A_0+K_0)/q,\quad U_2=(A_0+K_2)/\beta,\quad
 D=\mathcal L_V^{-1}(A_0I+K_1),\\
 H_0=\alpha+\rho+U_0,\quad H_2=\alpha+\rho+U_2,\quad
 \widehat H_1=\alpha I+D+\rho J-\rho\vartheta K.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
No extension of the metric at $q_0$ is asserted.
head: environment
name: Strong actual punctured PDE limit

title: Proof
body_md:
On the compact value/gradient/gap set established above, square root,
matrix inverse and scalar reciprocals have uniformly bounded finite
derivatives.  The Lyapunov eigenmultipliers are
$(v_i+v_j)/2\ge\delta_{V,K}$; its coefficient derivative is
$D(\mathcal L_V^{-1})[\dot V]=
-\mathcal L_V^{-1}\mathcal L_{\dot V}\mathcal L_V^{-1}$.
Thus the complete six real component equations have scalar principal
part and bounded right sides, smooth and uniformly Lipschitz in
coordinate/value/first-derivative arguments.
The local logarithmic potential of a bounded source has gradient
modulus $Ch(1+|\log h|)$: split the $1/r$ kernel at distance $2h$,
then integrate the far $h/r^2$ difference.  Bounded harmonic remainders
have interior differentiated Poisson estimates.  This gives uniform
$C^{1,\gamma}$ bounds for every $\gamma<1$.
The full right sides are now uniformly $C^{0,\gamma}$.  In their
Hessian potentials subtract the source value from the zero-angular-mean
$r^{-2}$ kernel.  The near integral is bounded by
$\int_0^r s^{\gamma-1}ds$; the far comparison is
$h\int_{2h}^R s^{\gamma-2}ds=O(h^\gamma)$.
The fixed-cutoff and harmonic terms are smooth.  These are the actual
local Poisson estimates of Lemma~\ref{common-local-potentials}; they
give uniform $C^{2,\gamma}$ bounds on smaller buffers.
Ascoli and lower-exponent interpolation, followed by a countable
exhaustion and diagonal subsequence, give the stated strong local limit.
All ordered sources, curvatures and covariant products then converge
strongly locally.

The explicit coefficient convergence of \eqref{lower-damping-limit}
passes the persistent damping
$-\rho J(F)+\rho\vartheta(I-J(F))$.
Since $\tau_n=t_n/\mu_s\to0$ and the mass is fixed, the rotated
original residual in \eqref{lower-polar-force} vanishes, leaving exactly
$A_0I$.  In coefficient coordinates the limiting equations are
\[
 \Delta A=H'_{*0}-\alpha-\rho-(A_0+K_0)/q,
 \quad\Delta B=c-\rho-(A_0+K_2)/\beta,
\]
\[
 \Delta F=g^{-1}F_{\bar z}F^{-1}F_z+dF
       +F[-\rho J(F)+\rho\vartheta(I-J(F))]
       -F^{1/2}\mathcal L_V^{-1}(A_0I+K_1)F^{1/2}.
\]
These give \eqref{lower-punctured-rows} after current-unitary transport.
All $X,Y$ reference terms are the derivatives of the displayed limiting
arrows with the limiting metrics; they remain at $p$ when $p\ne q_0$.
Local strong convergence identifies all source densities on fixed
punctured tests; inherited global budgets and monotone exhaustion
give finite punctured masses.  No global uniform integrability, removal,
or interchange of $n$ with puncture removal has been used.

label: lower-value-bound
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{lower-value-bound}
Fix the original rank-$(2,1,1)$ coefficient chain, background, reference,
one finite mass and slab as above.  Every normalized positive-symbol
$C^{2,\gamma}$ auxiliary solution with $0<\tau\le\tau_b$ obeys
\[
 \|a\|_\infty+\|b\|_\infty+\|M\|_{{\rm op},\infty}\le B_*.
\]
The bound is independent of $\tau$, the solution and its original
symbol minima; dependence on the fixed chain/reference/mass is allowed.
head: environment
name: Uniform values for every original lower-boundary chain

title: Proof
body_md:
If the solution family is empty the bound is vacuous.  Otherwise the
contradiction above gives a finite
$U_*:=\sup\overline{\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-M})}$: an infinite
supremum would let us choose actual solutions with means at least $n$,
the excluded sequence.
Set $D_-:=\max(0,U_*+C_-)$ and
$H_*=(C_T+D_-W)/\delta$, $\delta=4/21$.
Lemma~\ref{lower-mean-transfer} gives nonnegative shifted fields;
the reference-weight comparison gives
\[
 (a+D_-)+\operatorname{tr}(M+D_-I)+(b+D_-)\le H_*.
\]
Every summand and every shifted middle eigenvalue is bounded.
For instance $B_*=3(D_-+H_*)$ bounds the requested sum.
This reconstruction uses only the one scalar mean and applies to all
six unrestricted fields, including at $p$ and when $p=q_0$.

name: Original rank-one-lower existence

title: Proof
body_md:
For this zero-safe reference choose once
\[
 \mu_s\ge\max(t_{\rm req},T_{\rm all})/\tau_b,
\]
using the finite inverse, contraction and all-solution anchor constants
of Lemma~\ref{common-anchor}.  This is before choosing a positive stage
floor.  All coefficients there are smooth at $p$, including $D\psi(p)$,
and have no inverse lower norm.  Thus the independent full six-field
construction of Theorem~\ref{common-positive-continuation} supplies an
actual normalized smooth positive-symbol solution at every
$\tau\in(0,1]$, at this same fixed mass.  Its bounded-stage compact
map and component argument do not assume an original zero endpoint.

Theorem~\ref{lower-value-bound} supplies a parameter-uniform value
bound on the fixed positive-force slab.  The hypotheses of
Theorem~\ref{common-gradient-gaps} are now satisfied with this bound,
the same mass/reference and $c_1=A_0/2$.
That theorem gives global gradients and positive $q,\beta,V$ gaps
without a positive lower-arrow norm. Choose $\tau_n=\tau_b/(n+1)$
and a solution at each parameter. The same fixed reference and mass,
these global bounds and positive-parameter existence meet the hypotheses
of Theorem~\ref{common-original-endpoint}. Its ordered inverse is
$E_M^{-1}\mathcal L_V^{-1}$, with the Lyapunov inverse applied first.
All coefficients remain smooth at the lower zero, including $D\psi(p)$,
and at repeated middle spectra; none divides by the lower norm.
The theorem gives strong global $C^{2,\gamma}$ subsequence convergence,
the single normalization, smoothness, the undamped equation and strict
calibration on the original bundles. This application includes $p=q_0$.
Here the original values are bounded, so fixed mass makes both the
damping and reference-forcing terms vanish. In contrast, the escaping
punctured sequence had $t_nL_n\to\rho$, which produces the persistent
damping in \eqref{lower-punctured-rows}.
